data.title: Waskahigan Oil & Gas Corp. Announces Letter of Intent Regarding Business Combination with Private.Ki
data.description:
VANCOUVER, BC, Sept. 15, 2026 /CNW/ -- Waskahigan Oil & Gas Corp. ("Waskahigan" or the "Company") (), is pleased to announce that it has entered into a non-binding letter of intent dated September 14, 2026 (the "Letter of Intent"), with Private.Ki Ltd. ("Private.Ki") to complete a business combination transaction (the "Proposed Transaction").  Private.Ki provides an encrypted communication SuperApp unifying email, chat, and messenger in a single private space. The Proposed Transaction, if completed, will result in the business of Private.Ki becoming the business of the Company.

Completion of the Proposed Transaction remains subject to a number of conditions, including, but not limited to, completion of due diligence, negotiation and execution of a definitive transaction agreement (the "Definitive Agreement"), shareholder approval, Canadian Securities Exchange ("CSE") approval and the receipt of any other required approvals. The Proposed Transaction cannot be completed until these conditions are satisfied, and there can be no assurance that the Proposed Transaction will be completed at all.

The parties intend to apply for the listing for trading of the common shares of the issuer resulting from the Proposed Transaction (the "Resulting Issuer") on the CSE as of the effective time of completion of the Proposed Transaction (the "Closing Date"). In connection with the Proposed Transaction, the Company is contemplating a consolidation of its common shares on the basis of four pre-consolidation shares for one post-consolidation common share (the "Consolidation").

Pursuant to the Letter of Intent, the Company has agreed to pay CAD$2.5 million to the shareholders of Private.Ki (the "Target Shareholders") on the Closing Date with CAD$500,000 payable in cash and CAD$2 million payable by the issuance of post-Consolidation common shares of the Company (the "Consideration Shares") at $0.60 per Consideration Share. Subject to the achievement of certain business milestones by December 31, 2028, an additional CAD$14 million may be payable by the issuance of post-Consolidation shares on or before April 30, 2029 (the "Milestone Shares") at an issue price equal to the greater of $0.60 per Milestone Share and the minimum price permitted by the CSE at the time of issuance.

The parties also intend to complete an interim financing in connection with the Proposed Transaction, the terms of which have not been settled. The final details of the Proposed Transaction, Consolidation, purchase price, and interim financing will be settled and included in the Definitive Agreement. The parties are targeting execution of a Definitive Agreement by October 31, 2026.

The Proposed Transaction and the terms thereof were negotiated at arm's length. The Proposed Transaction is expected to constitute a "Fundamental Change" as defined in the policies of the CSE.

On completion of the Proposed Transaction, it is expected that the board of directors of the Resulting Issuer will consist of five (5) directors: Thomas Schroeter, Ross Ewaniuk, Jamil Kassam and two additional nominees of Private.Ki. Thomas Schroeter will be appointed Chief Executive Officer and President of the Resulting Issuer and Stephen Brohman will continue as Chief Financial Officer and Corporate Secretary. Ross Ewaniuk will resign as Interim Chief Executive Officer, and Stephen Brohman will resign as a director, in each case on completion of the Proposed Transaction. These appointments will be subject to acceptance by the CSE.

The full terms of the Proposed Transaction and the details of any interim financings required to complete the Proposed Transaction will be provided in future news releases in accordance with CSE policies.

About Private.Ki

Private.Ki Ltd. is a privately held corporation existing under the laws of the Republic of Seychelles. Private.Ki provides an encrypted communication SuperApp that unifies email, chat and messenger functionality in a single private space, bringing commonly used communication tools together within one private environment.

About Waskahigan Oil & Gas Corp.

Waskahigan Oil & Gas is a Canadian public company that is focused on identifying strategic mergers and acquisition opportunities with the goal of creating long-term value for shareholders through disciplined growth and responsible operations.

data.title: WSJ Tech Council Summit: NASA's Isaacman Wants Agency to Get Back Its Mojo
data.description:
By Elias Schisgall

Jared Isaacman wants the National Aeronautics and Space Administration to regain its mojo.

The NASA administrator said the agency has lost its focus and ability to quickly execute in recent years. "We are just trying to get our swagger back here, get back in a rhythm of what we did" in the 1960s, Isaacman said at The Wall Street Journal's Technology Council Summit, calling that period NASA's "glory days."

"This is simply going back to the playbook that achieved these near-impossible outcomes from decades past," Isaacman said.

There is urgency, he said, to breathe life into the agency as the U.S. races China to establish a presence on the moon and secure valuable lunar real estate.

"There is a second space race. It will come down to months, not years. The Chinese will absolutely put their astronauts on the surface of the Moon, do what the Soviets never could," Isaacman said. "And I think the implications of that will be felt around the world."

Isaacman has tried to realize this shift by eliminating "needless bureaucracy" and flattening the agency's organizational structure, as well as by spending more time in the field himself.

He is also trying to bring more of NASA's workforce back in-house, after what he described as an extended period of outsourcing to contractors that contributed to higher costs and slower launch cadences.

Personnel for mission control and rocket designing, construction and launching should be brought within the agency, Isaacman said. And though NASA should continue to act as one customer of many for components and services that have a high level of technical readiness, he said the agency should be more hands-on for more ambitious projects, such as spacecraft fueled by nuclear power.

"We are course-correcting back to center on the balance between, what is the near-impossible--it doesn't have an obvious business or use case--that NASA should be doing, and where can you leverage industry to supplement, just as we did in the early days," Isaacman said. "I think we're getting back to the right balance there."

data.title: Trump Threatens to Block Kennedy Center Renovations Over Naming Dispute — WSJ
data.description:
By Lydia Wheeler

The Kennedy Center's board voted to close the venue for a two-year renovation on Tuesday, but President Trump immediately threatened to block that work unless his name is restored to the building.

The president's threat came just hours after Judge Christopher Cooper in Washington, D.C. denied the latest attempt by the venue's board to affix an inscription that says "renovated and restored by Donald J. Trump" under President John F. Kennedy's name on the front portico, and to rename the center's grounds after Trump.

Shortly after Cooper's ruling, the board-stacked with Trump's own appointees, and chaired by the president himself-met, and passed a resolution to close the center for a two-year renovation.

Trump said in a social media post afterward that the venue will close immediately, but that the renovation can't begin until an appeals court rules on the board's approved name for the center. He signaled plans to go to the Supreme Court if he loses.

Cooper's decision Tuesday said the board's attempt to rename the venue violated the order he issued in May, which required Trump's name to be removed from the building-where the board had voted to add it in December. Only Congress has the authority to rename the institution, he ruled at the time.

"Simply put, Defendants cannot install memorials for President Trump or anyone or anything else at the Kennedy Center without Congress's blessing," wrote Cooper, an Obama appointee.

The board has argued the renovation can't be completed without honoring Trump and that there is nothing in the law that stops it from acknowledging his efforts to save the institution. It is Trump's name that is drawing in donations to repair the decimated building, which will have to be demolished if it can't be fixed, Justice Department attorneys told Cooper in court papers.

Cooper seemed to disregard that assertion, saying the board "offered no proof that current or future donations hinge on President Trump's name being on the building."

The ruling marked the latest twist in ongoing litigation over Trump's efforts to overhaul the iconic cultural art institution in Washington, D.C.

Trump has taken a keen interest in the Kennedy Center since taking office for his second term, among several renovation projects in and around the nation's capital, and has expressed frustration with the legal hurdles that his efforts to remake the institution-which he says is dangerously dilapidated and in dire financial straits-have met.

Trump joined the board's virtual meeting on Tuesday, along with Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, people familiar with the matter said. He expressed anger with Rep. Joyce Beatty, (D., Ohio), the ex-official board member who sued to get Trump's name taken off the building, calling her destructive, one of the people said.

The resolution the board passed, which was made public in a court filing Monday, said the building is in such disrepair that it is endangering visitors and employees, and that the consulting group hired for the renovation had recommended the closure.

Trump's name first went up on the building in December and came down a little over five months later. Scaffolding wrapped in a white tarp has covered much of the building's name ever since. The board said in court papers that it has been protecting the marble facade, which it suggested may have been damaged when Trump's name was taken down.

Beatty's attorneys hailed Cooper's ruling on Tuesday as "a victory for the memory of President Kennedy and for our nation."

"Two times the court has told President Trump the same thing: You are not above the law," Norm Eisen and Nathaniel Zelinsky said in a joint statement.

Write to Lydia Wheeler at lydia.wheeler@wsj.com

data.title: Bitcoin Falls After Senate Rejects Crypto-Friendly Bill — 2nd Update
data.description:
By Dean Seal and Farhan Rafid

Bitcoin and crypto stocks dropped Tuesday after the Senate blocked Trump-backed legislation that would've established an industry-friendly regulatory framework for cryptocurrencies and digital assets.

In the late afternoon, bitcoin was down 4.6% at around $75,633, according to CoinGlass. Shares of bitcoin holding company Strategy finished the trading day down 5.4% at $129.60. The crypto exchange Coinbase closed the day down 10% at $172.11.

Earlier Tuesday, the closely watched Clarity Act drafted by Senate Republicans fell short of the 60 yes votes it needed to be advanced to a formal floor vote, killing the bill's chances of getting passed ahead of November's midterm elections.

The loss, which came in a 49-to-50 vote, is a blow to the crypto industry as it wrangles with its deep financial connections to President Trump.

Senate Democrats had voiced concerns that the Clarity Act lacked safeguards against political self-dealing in the crypto industry. Sen. Elizabeth Warren, D-Mass., said ahead of the vote that the bill wouldn't prevent Trump from continuing to profit from his own crypto ventures while using his political power to boost the industry.

The bill was pushed by Sen. Cynthia Lummis, R-Wyo., chair for the Senate Banking Digital Assets Subcommittee, who said the latest draft included ethics provisions that Trump had agreed to, along with more than 100 other concessions secured by Democrats after years of bipartisan negotiations, Lummis said at a conference on Monday.

"This is not a partisan bill, not even close," Lummis told senators before the vote on Tuesday.

Democrats ultimately rallied against the measure, including Sen. Kirsten Gillibrand of New York, who has worked with Lummis on crypto legislation and was praised by Lummis on Monday for her help in moving the Clarity Act forward. Four Republicans joined the Democrats in dissent.

Prediction-market traders have been persistently skeptical about legislation making it across the finish line this year. Polymarket put the probability of the Clarity Act becoming law in 2026 at 31% Monday morning, its highest level all month. That probability fell to 5% on Tuesday.

Polymarket has a data sharing partnership with Dow Jones, publisher of Dow Jones Newswires and the Wall Street Journal.

The loss puts pressure on crypto prices after a rally this past summer, driven in part by optimism around the bill along with currency devaluation fears.

Bitcoin rose around 25% between Aug. 19 and Aug. 25, and climbed above $82,000 at the start of September before pulling back. Investors have recently viewed $80,000 as an opportunity to sell, said Stephen Coltman, head of macro at 21Shares.

Investors are also still awaiting the Federal Reserve's interest-rate decision Wednesday. Analysts have pointed to the Fed decision as a potential catalyst for bitcoin as it struggles to regain the $80,000 level.

Write to Dean Seal at dean.seal@wsj.com

data.title: ComEd, League of Chicago Theatres Award $205,000 in Grants to Support the Arts
data.description:
ComEd and the League of Chicago Theatres today announced the recipients of the 2026 Powering the Arts Grant Program. Celebrating its ninth year, the program is awarding a total of $205,000 to 19 nonprofit organizations across northern Illinois. These funds will support a range of arts initiatives, from youth creative development to engaging community experiences.

“ComEd is proud to partner with the League of Chicago Theatres to support local arts programs that enrich our neighborhoods,” said Melissa Washington, senior vice president of Government, Regulatory and External Affairs at ComEd. “This year’s recipients continue to advance that mission. Each project celebrates the vibrancy of our communities, and they collectively expand access to live performances, music education, community festivals and opportunities for creative expression for the people we serve.”

Since its launch in 2018, the Powering the Arts Grant Program has awarded nearly $1.5 million in grant funding to support over 150 different arts and cultural projects within the ComEd service territory. ComEd and the League of Chicago Theatres work closely together to administer the program. Grant applications are reviewed by an external panel of judges, and grant recipients match the award funding with their own investment of equal or greater value towards their project.

“Arts and culture enrich our neighborhoods and play an essential role in building thriving communities,” said Executive Director of the Chicago League of Theatres Marissa Lynn Jones. “As we enter the 2027 grant season, our ongoing partnership with ComEd reflects a shared commitment to strengthening the arts sector and expanding access to creative experiences across our region. By supporting local arts organizations, we are helping them deepen their community impact, engage new audiences, and contribute to more vibrant, connected, and resilient communities.”

ComEd remains committed to working with local organizations to invest in projects that improve quality of life for northern Illinois residents. The Powering the Arts Grant Program is one of ComEd’s four Power for Good grant programs empowering communities across northern Illinois together with the Powering Safe Communities Grant Program, the Green Region Grant Program and the Powering the Holidays Grant Program.

More information about ComEd grant opportunities is available at ComEd.com/Grants.

The 2026 ComEd Powering the Arts Grant Program recipients and their funded projects include:

Paramount Arts Centre, Inc (Aurora) will expand its programming that creates meaningful opportunities to experience live theater with more targeted theater engagement events serving more than 500 Aurora educators, nurses, first responders, veterans and seniors.

Mandi Theater (Buffalo Grove) will expand its accessibility initiative throughout its 10th Annual International Theatre Festival by removing financial, linguistic, and engagement barriers.

John Walt Foundation (Chicago, Austin) will expand its six-week Summer Apprenticeship Program, providing 20 to 25 West Side youth with paid creative arts and workforce development opportunities.

The Chicago Mosaic School (Chicago, Edgewater) will relaunch its Teaching the Teachers program, providing affordable mosaic arts training to approximately 200 local educators who collectively serve more than 3,000 students.

The World Music Foundation (Chicago, Edgewater) will present 22 live world music sessions for approximately 660 seniors and families, bringing global music experiences directly to those living in Chicago affordable housing communities.

UrbanTheater Company (Chicago, Humboldt Park) will launch Cruzando Generaciones (Crossing Generations), a weekend theater workshop series for Humboldt Park and surrounding area high school students that connects teens and older adults through theater, storytelling and oral history.

Uniting Voices (Chicago, Hyde Park) will expand upon and launch new North Lawndale school programs to provide choral instruction and performance opportunities impacting up to 300 students.

Culture Shock Chicago NFP (Chicago, Lincoln Park) will expand its Shockwaves hip-hop arts program to rural northern Illinois schools and communities who currently have limited arts access, reaching approximately 3,000 students and community members.

Young People's Theatre of Chicago (Chicago, Lincoln Park) will launch the Student Access Initiative aimed at expanding access to live theater for approximately 1,500 students from 25 Chicago Public Schools through free tickets and transportation assistance.

Midnight Circus in the Parks (Chicago, Lincoln Square) will bring four free circus performances, interactive juggling activities and dedicated transportation from a local senior center to Brighton Park, providing access for up to 1,600 attendees.

Villapalooza Inc. (Chicago, Little Village) will expand its free Little Village Arts and Music Festival that includes local and national artists, community resources and ongoing public engagement, reaching more than 3,000 attendees.

The Joffrey Ballet (Chicago, Loop) will present Joffrey for All, a free outdoor dance performance at Gallagher Way expected to reach up to 3,000 people.

Project H.O.O.D. (Chicago, South Side) will launch its first dedicated theater and performing arts program which will provide 40 to 60 children in Englewood and Woodlawn with free theater training before a public community showcase.

TimeLine Theatre Company (Chicago, Uptown) will provide Chicago teens with a free six-week summer program combining theater training, professional mentorship and a paid opportunity to create original performances.

Illinois Conservatory for the Arts (DuPage) will launch the IMPACT Access Initiative to provide free or low-cost performing arts opportunities to approximately 250 students and create pathways into scholarships, return events and audition preparation.

Elgin Youth Symphony Orchestra, Inc. (Elgin) will provide free after-school violin and viola instruction and instruments to fourth-grade students across the Fox Valley region.

Angels Athletics (Flossmoor) will expand its Angels in the Arts programming through artist workshops, cultural outings, dance and an intergenerational musical production serving youth, families and seniors.

Freeport Art Museum (Freeport) will expand Paint the Port to include more live music and additional sponsored painting opportunities for approximately 1,500 participants and visitors.

Spotlight Performance Academy (Homewood) will launch a new senior community choir in Homewood and Flossmoor, engaging at least 60 seniors in music and intergenerational performances.

data.title: AP sues to challenge limits on access to US lawsuits by immigration detainees
data.description:
By Nate Raymond

The Associated Press sued the U.S. federal judiciary on Tuesday to challenge the constitutionality of a rule that has restricted reporters' ability to easily access lawsuits by people detained as part of President Donald Trump's immigration crackdown.

The news service in a lawsuit filed in a federal court in Washington, D.C., said thousands of people arrested during Trump's efforts to ramp up deportations have filed cases alleging they ​were unlawfully detained.

Like other media outlets, the AP said that it has sought to report on the so-called habeas cases "due to the immense public interest in the federal government’s immigration enforcement policies and the treatment of detainees in its custody."

"But over and over, AP reporters have met a roadblock that substantially impedes AP’s ability to report on these immigration habeas cases in a timely fashion, and in some respects prevents covering these cases at all," the lawsuit said.

The lawsuit challenges a provision of the Federal Rules of Civil Procedure that restricts remote electronic access to documents filed in immigration-related cases, preventing them from being downloaded from the online court records system known as the Public Access to Court Electronic Records, or PACER.

While such records are public, they can only be accessed usually by going to the courthouse where they are filed and requesting access in person through a clerk's office, where they can often be viewed on a public terminal.

The AP argues that under the U.S. Constitution's First Amendment, those records are subject to a qualified right of access and should be available via PACER like other court documents.

It said the rule also constitutes an unconstitutional content-based restriction because it restricts access to filings based solely on a case's subject matter, in this case immigration.

"The result — even if unintentional — is that immigrants’ claims of unlawful detention by the federal government are much less visible to the public than other kinds of federal lawsuits," the lawsuit contends.

The lawsuit names as a defendant the Administrative Office of the U.S. Courts, the judiciary's administrative arm. A spokesperson for the Administrative Office declined to comment.

The lawsuit was filed by lawyers at the Reporters Committee for Freedom of the Press, which in May separately asked the U.S. Judicial Conference's Committee on Rules of Practice and Procedure to revise the rule to remove the restrictions on electronic access to the immigration-related records.

The proposed rule change has been referred to a Judicial Conference advisory committee, which next meets on October 21. Any change, though, would likely take years to wind through the judiciary's usual rulemaking process.

The case is The Associated Press v. Administrative Office of the U.S. Courts, U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia, No. 1:26-cv-03219.

For the AP: Renee Griffin and Adam Marshall of the Reporters Committee for Freedom of the Press

data.title: HeartSciences reports FQ1 2027 net loss $3.2M; shareholders' deficit $2.0M
data.description:
HeartSciences reported a net loss of $3.2 million for the fiscal first quarter ended July 31, 2026, and no meaningful revenue for the period. Loss from operations was $2.9 million, and the company recorded a $0.3 million inventory reserve related to its wavECG device. As of July 31, 2026, HeartSciences had a shareholders’ deficit of $2.0 million and has since raised additional capital through equity sales and ATM offerings.

Financial Highlights

  • Revenue: No meaningful revenue reported for FQ1 2027.
  • Loss from operations: $2.9 million for FQ1 2027 (FQ1 2026: $1.9 million).
  • Net loss: $3.2 million for FQ1 2027 (FQ1 2026: $2.1 million).
  • Inventory reserve: $0.3 million reserve recorded against wavECG-related inventory.
  • Shareholders’ deficit: $2.0 million as of July 31, 2026; subsequent financings raised approximately $1.0 million from Fortitude and approximately $1.2 million net from ATM sales.

Business Highlights

  • Proposed transaction: Continued progress toward a business combination with Fortitude, expected to close in Q4 calendar 2026 subject to customary conditions and shareholder approval.
  • MyoVista Insights commercial traction: First U.S. commercial agreements signed following full launch and selection as the AI-ECG delivery platform for a clinical program at a major European reference center with potential to expand to a multicenter project.
  • Platform upgrades and marketplace: MyoVista Insights reached version 1.4 and added the first third-party FDA-cleared AI-ECG algorithm to its marketplace, enabling cloud-based delivery of AI algorithms into clinical workflows.
  • Intellectual property and marketing: Continued expansion of patent portfolio (now more than 45 granted patents) and launch of a new corporate website centered on MyoVista Insights.
  • wavECG device status: FDA 510(k) submission remains under review; company does not plan significant additional investment in device commercialization given regulatory, R&D, and commercial considerations and the shift toward cloud-based AI-ECG delivery.

Original SEC Filing: HeartSciences Inc. [ HSCS ] - 8-K - Sep. 15, 2026
